title: Helm upgrade ordering + readiness gates for Private (control plane before data plane)
creator: Connor O'Brien
body:
Context
Private upgrades have historically been fragile when chart changes roll out in a non-deterministic order (e.g., dataplane DaemonSets/Deployments restart while control plane API/migrations are still in-flight). This ticket coordinates Helm chart changes to enforce a safe upgrade ordering and provide explicit readiness gates/timeouts that align with the installer upgrade plan (CP -> DP) and rollback semantics.

Goal
Make an in-place upgrade deterministic and safe-by-default:
1) Control plane components upgrade and become Ready first
2) Only then do data plane components roll
3) Pre-upgrade jobs run (when required) with explicit timeouts and clear failure messages
4) Helm rollback does not leave the cluster in a worse state (no destructive hooks; idempotent jobs)

Scope
- redwood-helm-charts: split upgrade into explicit phases (CP and DP)
- Add pre-upgrade hook jobs with stable ordering + timeouts
- Add readiness gates that the installer can rely on (and that operators can reason about)
- Ensure hooks are idempotent and rollback-safe

Non-goals
- Full blue/green chart strategy (rejected in ADR)
- Automating multi-hop major upgrades (N-1 -> N only for GA path)

Proposed behavior (operator-facing)
- Operator runs installer upgrade; installer will upgrade charts in phases.
- Phase 1 (control plane): helm upgrade for control-plane chart(s) only.
  - Pre-upgrade checks/migrations jobs run (if required) with bounded timeouts.
  - Upgrade blocks until control plane readiness gate passes.
- Phase 2 (data plane): helm upgrade for data-plane chart(s).
  - Data plane rollouts have bounded timeouts; failure leaves control plane stable.

Implementation details
1) Hook ordering
- Use Helm hooks with deterministic ordering and explicit weights:
  - pre-upgrade: run schema-guard / compatibility-check jobs (weight -10)
  - pre-upgrade: run “config reconcile” job (weight -5) (no mutations that can’t be rolled back)
  - post-upgrade: run “smoke/health verification” job (weight +5)
- Ensure hook delete policy does not hide useful failure evidence:
  - Keep failed jobs/pods around for debugging (hook-succeeded delete; do not delete on failure)

2) Timeouts
- Default hook job timeouts:
  - Compatibility/preflight hook: 5m
  - Migration guard job (if used as a hook): 20m (must be aligned with DB migration lock timeout defaults)
  - Post-upgrade verification: 10m
- Helm upgrade timeout should be explicitly configured in installer; charts should also have sensible defaults for per-component rollout timeouts.

3) Readiness gates
- Define a CP readiness gate that the installer can query:
  - Control plane API Deployment Ready
  - Controller/worker pods Ready
  - “/healthz” and “/readyz” endpoints returning success
  - No pending critical migrations (exposed as a configmap/condition or a health endpoint flag)
- Define a DP readiness gate:
  - DP gateway / router Deployment Ready
  - DP model-runtime pods Ready (as applicable)
  - Ability to reach CP API (simple connectivity check in post-upgrade job)

4) Rollback-safe behavior
- No hook should irreversibly mutate state without the backup/rollback mechanism being able to restore.
- If migrations are required:
  - Ensure they are backward compatible for one version where possible.
  - If not possible, chart hooks must fail fast and clearly indicate “manual intervention required” and point to the rollback runbook.

Acceptance criteria
- CP and DP rollouts are separated such that DP does not roll until CP readiness gate passes.
- Helm hook ordering is deterministic (weights) and documented in chart NOTES.
- Pre-upgrade hook jobs have explicit resource requests/limits and timeouts.
- Failure modes are actionable:
  - Hook failure prints remediation guidance (where to look in logs, common causes).
- End-to-end test (ENG-4877) covers: N-1 -> N upgrade with simulated CP delay; DP should not roll early.
- Works for both VPC and on-prem packaging (no reliance on external connectivity in hooks).

Links / artifacts
- GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR-2190 “add pre-upgrade job ordering and timeouts”
- GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR-2204 “split control-plane and data-plane rollout phases”
- Related: redwood-private-installer plan generator + phase execution (ENG-4821)

Progress updates
2025-03-06 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Drafted chart changes plan. Proposed split into two charts (cp + dp) to make installer orchestration explicit. Connor + Ethan aligned that this is easier to reason about than trying to gate within a single chart via hooks.

2025-03-12 (Connor O'Brien)
- Review note: make sure hook delete policies keep failed jobs for support bundles; we’ve lost evidence in past incidents.
- Ask: align migration job timeouts with new DB lock timeout defaults from platform migration guardrails.

2025-03-19 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Opened PR-2190 with hook weights + initial timeouts.
- Added NOTES output describing the phase expectations and where to check job logs.

2025-03-26 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Opened PR-2204 splitting cp/dp rollout phases.
- Added minimal “cp-ready” verification job (post-upgrade) that checks CP service endpoint and required deployments are Ready.

2025-04-02 (Rafael Mendes)
- SRE feedback: ensure dp post-upgrade verification includes CP connectivity check AND dp router readiness; also set rollout timeouts so we don’t hang indefinitely during an incident.

2025-04-08 (Sahana Iyer)
- Ran early integration suite in staging; found one issue: dp pods started rolling during cp chart upgrade because dp chart was included in umbrella chart install. Fix: remove dp from umbrella default upgrade path; installer should explicitly upgrade dp chart only after cp succeeds.

2025-04-11 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Merged PR-2190 + PR-2204.
- Verified via local Kind + internal staging: dp upgrade step does not begin until cp readiness gate passes.
- Documented required installer behavior: run helm upgrades separately (cp then dp), and set helm timeout >= sum of hook timeouts.

Open follow-ups
- Ensure installer explicitly sets helm timeout in both phases and captures hook job logs for support bundle (tracked in ENG-4899).
- Confirm default resource limits for hook jobs won’t starve small on-prem clusters; may need configurable values (file a follow-up if design partners hit this).

Decision log
- Rejected: single chart with complex intra-chart gating. Chosen: split cp/dp phases aligned to installer upgrade plan for determinism + simpler rollback reasoning.

QA / verification checklist
- [x] Upgrade N-1 -> N on staging (VPC) with artificial CP rollout delay; dp did not begin until cp gate passed.
- [x] Hook job failure retains artifacts for debugging.
- [x] Rollback from dp phase failure leaves cp stable and operator can retry dp phase after remediation.

Notes for Support
If an upgrade fails:
- First check hook jobs in the namespace for failures (compatibility-check, reconcile, verify).
- If failure occurs in CP phase: do not proceed to DP. Recommend rollback only after confirming backups (see runbook).
- If failure occurs in DP phase: CP should remain stable; capture dp job logs + pod events and advise retry after remediation.
